design_assessment: Three-tier rate limiting: (1) global API limiter `throttle:api` applied to entire api middleware group (Kernel.php:55) — 120 req/min default per user/IP (config app.api_throttle_per_minute); (2) named limiters for specific buckets: admin-mutation (300 GET, 30 POST except POS at 120, login-lockout 10/10min, kiosk-login 30/min, kiosk-orders 5/min, pos-order-create 60/min, oss-public 60/min); (3) hot-endpoint-specific throttles `throttle:N,M` inline on individual routes (forgot-password 3,60 + 5,1 stages, signup 5,1, csp-report 1000,1, etc.). The pattern is well-layered and each bucket has documented rationale (BLUE 2026-05-08 separate availability throttle, iter15-BUG-RATE-LIMIT POS lift, Sprint H5-B oss-public per-IP). Per-IP keying is correctly restored post Wave 3 P1.

sre_concerns.finding: Per-IP throttle effectiveness depends on TrustProxies::$proxies='*' AND nginx forwarding X-Forwarded-For correctly. If a future deploy adds a CDN (CloudFlare, CloudFront) between client and nginx, the X-Forwarded-For chain becomes `client-ip, cf-ip` and Laravel's getClientIp() may resolve to cf-ip (the LAST entry in the chain) instead of client-ip (the FIRST). Symfony's Request::getClientIp() returns the LEFTMOST trusted entry — with $proxies='*' trusting everyone, this works correctly. But if the chain becomes 3-deep + a misconfigured intermediate, weird things happen. P2 because today's deployment is single-restaurant local with no CDN. RECOMMEND adding a sentinel `TrustProxiesIPResolutionSentinelTest` that asserts `Request::create('/', 'GET', ['REMOTE_ADDR' => '127.0.0.1', 'HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR' => '1.2.3.4, 5.6.7.8'])->ip()` returns '1.2.3.4' (the leftmost client IP).
sre_concerns.remediation: Defer to V1.0.2. Today's local deploy is safe.

sre_concerns.finding: Item photo upload POST /api/admin/items/{id}/photo lacks a dedicated throttle. Inherits admin-mutation 30/min (since it's NOT under /api/admin/pos/*). A catalog manager uploading 10 product photos triggers 429 after ~30 uploads. UX impact: admin must wait 60s between bursts. Low severity because catalog edits are infrequent ops.
sre_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — declare a `catalog-upload` named limiter at 60/min, or move photo upload route to /api/admin/items/* under a separate child group with higher throttle.

sre_concerns.finding: Inline route-level throttle `throttle:60,1` syntax (used 8+ times: csp-report 1000,1, signup paths 3,5/5,1/10,1, loyalty 10,1, etc.) creates ad-hoc limiters that are NOT keyed consistently. Laravel's default `throttle:60,1` keys by user_id || ip — same as the named limiters. BUT the response shape on 429 differs: named limiters with `->response(function() {...})` return a custom JSON shape (e.g., kiosk-orders returns `{message, retry_after}`), while ad-hoc `throttle:60,1` returns Laravel's default HTML 429 page. For an API consumer this is inconsistent.
sre_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — promote each ad-hoc throttle to a named limiter with explicit JSON 429 response. Consistency play.

sre_concerns.finding: RateLimiter `oss-public` is the ONLY rate limiter on the unauthenticated /api/frontend/oss-order surface — 60/min/IP across BOTH endpoints (index + popular-items). A fleet of 5 wall-displays behind one NAT polls every 5-10s — ~12 req/min × 2 endpoints = 24 req/min. Fits with headroom. BUT: the SHARED `throttle:api` middleware on the api group ALSO applies (120/min/IP default). The TIGHTER (oss-public) takes effect. Verified intact. Logging of >10 distinct branch_id values from same IP within 5 min was deferred to V1.0.2 per inline doc — sweep-detection sentinel is missing.
sre_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — implement the branch_id sweep-detection sentinel. Audit log when same IP hits >10 distinct branch_ids on /oss-order within 5min window.

sre_concerns.finding: RateLimiter `api` default uses `Limit::perMinute(perMinute)->by(user_id || ip)` — when user_id is present, the limit is shared across ALL endpoints. A cashier on POS V4 generating ~100 req/min for the menu+pricing preview workflow could starve their own /api/admin/dashboard polling for stats. Mitigated by per-bucket overrides (pos-quote 120/min, admin-mutation GET 300/min) but the parent throttle:api still applies and uses min(parent, child). Today: parent=120, admin-mutation-GET=300 → effective 120 cashier-wide. Wide enough for normal POS use.
sre_concerns.remediation: No change. Document the min(parent, child) semantics in plans/PROJECT_BRAIN.md §11.

sre_concerns.finding: Idempotency middleware fail_open config (config/idempotency.php:23) — `IDEMPOTENCY_FAIL_OPEN` env defaults to false. When Redis is unhealthy AND a required-route POST arrives with X-Idempotency-Key, the middleware returns 503 (per IdempotencyKeyRepository fail mode). On a single-restaurant deployment with no Redis, this is critical for kiosk: pos-order-create + frontend order POST would 503 on every Redis hiccup. The fallback path mentions an `app-layer UNIQUE backstop` in middleware docstring (L24-25), but routing 503s upstream is a hard fail for the cashier. Production posture should be `IDEMPOTENCY_FAIL_OPEN=true` for a single-restaurant local deploy.
sre_concerns.remediation: Verify .env.example posture. Production .env in single-restaurant should set IDEMPOTENCY_FAIL_OPEN=true. Add deployment doc note.

evidence.per_ip_throttle_via_trust_proxies: TrustProxies $proxies='*' (verified line 24) + Symfony Request::getClientIp() returns the leftmost trusted entry from X-Forwarded-For. Pre-heal (Wave 3 P0 SYNC-ADV3-01) had $proxies=null which made $request->ip() return the nginx loopback for every caller. Heal restored per-attacker keying.
